conflicts: Real-world figures are spreads from several sources and are kept side by side, never averaged; the maker interval is always given with them.
not_found: Brake pad life in hours: no public engine-builder, magazine or two-agreeing owner source with hour figures was found; makers say inspect every race and replace as required.
Wheel bearing and linkage/swingarm bearing replacement hours: makers publish inspection and greasing intervals only; no two agreeing public real-world hour figures were found.
Spark plug real-world life: makers publish intervals (e.g. Kawasaki 7.5 h, KTM two-strokes 15 h); no independent hour figures found.

Honda CRF450R/CRF250R 2020-on and Kawasaki KX450/KX250 2020-on: no two agreeing public reports with hours for how often the valves actually tighten on these generations (older-generation Honda titanium-valve reports exist but do not apply). Some owner-forum pages could not be read and were not used.

records.statement: Kawasaki schedules new piston and rings every 6 races (or 15 hours). An engine shop that builds motocross and enduro engines publishes 15-30 hours for 250F and 450F pistons and rings in race use, and notes modern makers ask for a piston at about 15 hours or 5-6 races. Riding type: amateur and pro motocross racing.

values.maker_interval: new piston and rings every 6 races (or 15 hours)

source.name: Moto-House MX engine shop, scheduled maintenance and rebuilds page

records.statement: Kawasaki schedules new piston and rings every 6 races (or 15 hours). In real use, testers and parts dealers put a 250F piston at about 25-40 hours for an amateur racer and a 450F at about 30-60 hours, with some 450 pistons run 100 hours as a gamble; a pro should change a 450 piston by about 20 hours. Owners racing at local level report 30-50 hours. Riding type: pro race vs amateur race; trail riders are not covered and often go longer. Measure ring gap, skirt and bore rather than assume.

values.maker_interval: new piston and rings every 6 races (or 15 hours)

source.name: Motocross Action, The tortured life of a piston

records.notes: Spread kept as published: one source says 250F 40 h and 450F 60 h for non-pros; another says 25-30 h for a raced 250F and 30-40 h for a 450.

records.statement: Kawasaki schedules crankshaft inspection every 6 races (or 15 hours). An engine shop says a well-maintained four-stroke crank can see 150-200 hours and should be inspected at every top end; a parts dealer says a four-stroke bottom end typically lasts about 100 hours but most riders rebuild at about 80 hours, with a fresh top end at the same time. Riding type: amateur race and general use.

real_world_hours.dealer: about 100 h, often done at about 80 h

source.name: Moto-House MX engine shop, scheduled maintenance and rebuilds page

records.notes: A dealer figure supports the engine shop figure; both agree the bottom end lasts several top ends.

also_sources.name: MXstore guide, When should I rebuild my dirt bike engine

records.statement: Kawasaki schedules a valve-clearance inspection every 6 races (or 15 hours). Mechanics and owners widely agree that a valve clearance that keeps getting tighter means the valve face or seat is wearing (titanium intakes most often), that the time between adjustments then gets shorter, and that the lasting fix is new valves with the seats cut, usually new springs too, rather than repeated shims. Riding type: all; dirty air filters and running on the rev limiter speed it up.

values.maker_interval: a valve-clearance inspection every 6 races (or 15 hours)
values.sign: clearance moving tighter at each check; hard starting

source.name: Vital MX forum, Drastic valve adjustment (KX450)

records.notes: A valve maker also recommends a complete new valve and spring kit for engines at or past factory service limits.

records.topic: how often racers change the oil
records.statement: Kawasaki schedules engine oil every 6 races (or 15 hours). Racers and owners commonly change engine oil much sooner, about every 3-5 hours or every race day, and some every ride on bikes where engine, gearbox and clutch share the oil; the oil filter is often done every second change. Riding type: amateur race and practice.

source.name: Vital MX forum, Oil change intervals...manufacturer recommendations

also_sources.name: Vital MX forum, 2023-24 Yamaha YZ450 engine hours/longevity

records.statement: Kawasaki schedules fork oil every 6 races (or 15 hours) and shock oil every 6 races (or 15 hours). A suspension columnist services a hard-ridden practice bike every 10-15 hours, while a European suspension dealer quotes 20-40 hours depending on the bike; both say sand, hard riding and fast riders shorten it. Oil is usually the last thing to wear; bushings, seals, piston bands and shims go first. Signs: you keep going stiffer and slower on the clickers and they do less. Riding type: race and practice.

values.maker_interval: fork oil every 6 races (or 15 hours) and shock oil every 6 races (or 15 hours)

source.name: Motocross Action suspension column, when to service your fork and shock

records.statement: Kawasaki schedules a chain and sprocket wear inspection after each race (or 2.5 hours). Riders report a sealed (O- or X-ring) chain lasting about 50-100 hours with care, while plain chains and hard motocross use wear one out in about 20-50 hours; steel rear sprockets outlast aluminium ones, the countershaft sprocket wears first, and dealers advise replacing chain and sprockets together. Riding type: amateur motocross and trail.

values.maker_interval: a chain and sprocket wear inspection after each race (or 2.5 hours)

source.name: Vital MX forum, whats the deal on chain life

also_sources.name: MXstore guide, When to replace your dirt bike chain

records.statement: The maker gives no tire hour figure. Riders on 450s and 250Fs report a rear knobby lasting roughly 8-25 hours and a front roughly 15-30 hours on motocross tracks, with slower riders and trail use getting 40 hours or more; fronts last much longer than rears, and flipping a tire extends its life by about a quarter. Riding type: motocross race and practice vs trail.

riding_type.motocross race/practice: rear about 8-25 h, front about 15-30 h

source.name: Vital MX forum, Average number of hours you are getting on rear and front tires
